name: Sideways
description: Around this tube is a solenoid: switch on its supply (the yellow coil at the top right) to fill the tube with a magnetic field along its length, out of the board when positive. Electrons crossing it curve, and above a critical field (Hull's cutoff) they cannot reach the anode at all: they drift along the cathode instead, sideways, perpendicular to both the electric and the magnetic field. Send the electrons into the collector above the gap: at least 0.9 must land there (averaged over $t = 20$ to $40$).

reality.represents: Hull's magnetic cutoff: the magnetron's principle

remarks.detail: Above a field of about √(2V m/q)/d the electrons curve back before the anode and drift along the cathode, at E/B across both fields.
Below the cutoff a little current still reaches the anode at the gap's ends, where the translation symmetry behind Hull's theorem is broken.

The tube is the same all along its length: its electrodes are long prisms, its electrons long lines of charge, its currents per unit length. A real tube is a few centimetres long and has end effects; the textbooks' planar and coaxial laws assume this symmetry too.

remarks.line: A uniform field from the solenoid
remarks.detail: The solenoid round the tube makes an exactly uniform field along it; a real magnet's field is only nearly uniform.
